metaDescription: NeakGuard is a Windows app that spots disguised Telegram Desktop Attachments, such as archives that hide programs. It works alongside Microsoft Defender and is not an antivirus.
heroTitle: That PDF might be a program.
heroLead: NeakGuard spots disguised Telegram Attachments and moves them to Quarantine.
screensLead: The App lists every Attachment in Quarantine. Restore one only if you trust who sent it.
altHomeKm: The NeakGuard App in Khmer. It lists Attachments in Quarantine, each with a Restore button.
altHomeEn: The NeakGuard App in English. It lists Attachments in Quarantine, each with a Restore button.
step1Text: You confirm a Watched Folder, usually where Telegram Desktop saves what you receive. NeakGuard watches only that folder.
step2Text: A Finding is one clear reason an Attachment looks disguised.
findingExample: Looks like a PDF but is a Windows program
step1Point2: Usually the Telegram Desktop download folder
step1Point3: Change the folder in the App at any time
step2Point1: Checks the real format, not only the name
step2Point2: Looks inside archives for hidden programs
step2Point3: An Uninspected Attachment always comes with a reason
step3Point2: Restore puts the file back without overwriting anything
step3Point3: Only you can Delete a file in Quarantine
step3Text: An Attachment with a Finding is Suspicious. NeakGuard moves it to Quarantine, so you cannot open it by accident. If you are sure you trust the sender, you can Restore it.
noteText: NeakGuard is not an antivirus and does not replace one. Keep Microsoft Defender on.
noteNoFindings: When NeakGuard reports No Findings, it examined the Attachment and found nothing. That never means the file is safe.
faq1A: No. NeakGuard works alongside antivirus software and never replaces it. Keep Microsoft Defender on.
faq2A: Attachments that appear in your Watched Folder, usually the Telegram Desktop download folder. It looks for disguises, such as an archive that hides a program or a file whose real format differs from its name. If NeakGuard cannot finish, for example because an archive has a password, it marks the Attachment Uninspected and tells you why.
faq3Q: What happens to a Suspicious Attachment?
faq3A: NeakGuard moves it to Quarantine automatically. You can Restore it, and it returns to where it came from without overwriting anything. NeakGuard never deletes a quarantined Attachment on its own. Delete is always your choice.
faq4Q: Where does NeakGuard examine my files?
faq4A: On your computer. For each Attachment, NeakGuard starts a short-lived, sandboxed process called the Inspector. The Inspector can read the file, but it can never move, change or delete it.
faq5A: Only the NeakGuard App is open source. The Broker, which watches folders and owns the Quarantine, and the Inspector are not. A build of the App from its source does not watch folders or examine Attachments. To get protection, install a NeakGuard release.
